text: προετοιμάζω, I prepare beforehand.
προευαγγελίζομαι, I proclaim the good news beforehand.
gloss: I proclaim the good news beforehand

text: προέχω, I excel, surpass; pass. in Rom. iii 9.
προηγέομαι, I lead in front, I give a lead to.
gloss: I lead in front, I give a lead to

text: προθεσμία, a term (or age, date) previously indicated (fixed, laid down).
gloss: a term (or age, date) previously indicated

text: πρόθυμος, eager: in Rom. i 15 τὸ κατ᾽ ἐμὲ πρόθυμον may be = ἡ ἐμὴ προθυμία, my good will, but perhaps it is better to read πρόθυμος (sc. εἰμί) with some authorities.
προθύμως, eagerly.
πρόϊμος (not πρώϊμος, but from πρό), early in the year (understand ὑετός or some other word meaning rain): reference is to that beginning in October: opposed to ὄψιμος.
προκαλέομαι, I call out, challenge.
προκαταγγέλλω, I announce beforehand.
προκαταρτίζω, I prepare (arrange) beforehand.
προκηρύσσω, I proclaim previously.
προκοπή, progress, advance.
προκόπτω (originally of the pioneer cutting his way through brushwood), I advance, progress, make progress.
πρόκριμα, prejudgement (favourable or unfavourable).
προκυρόω, I make valid beforehand.

προλαμβάνω, (a) I take before another (perhaps); I am in a hurry to take, I take eagerly, I seize, 1 Cor. xi 21; (b) προέλαβεν μυρίσαι, has by anticipation anointed (perhaps an Aramaism), Mk. xiv 8; (c) (deprehendo) I catch, capture, overtake (before he can escape).
προμαρτύρομαι, I call (God) beforehand to witness.
προμελετάω, I practise beforehand, I prepare, I get up.
gloss: I practise beforehand, I prepare, I get up

text: προμεριμνάω, I am anxious beforehand.
προνοέω, act. and mid., I take thought for beforehand, I provide for.
gloss: I take thought for beforehand, I provide for

text: πρόνοια, forethought, foresight; πρόνοιαν ποιοῦμαι = προνοέω.
προοράω, I see beforehand, I foresee, I see previously, Ac. xxi 29: mid. I pay regard to, set before me, Ac. ii 25.
gloss: I see beforehand, I foresee, I see previously

text: προορίζω, I foreordain (lit. I bound [limit] beforehand).
προπάσχω, I suffer previously.
προπάτωρ, a forefather.

προπέμπω, (a) I send in front (forth, forward), set forward, start on their way (in Tit. iii 13, of being provided with necessaries for the journey); (b) (prosequor), I convey, I escort on (his, &c.) way, as a mark of affection and respect, Ac. xv 3, xx 38, xxi 5, Rom. xv 24, 3 John 6.
gloss: I send in front (forth, forward), set forward
note: punctuation after 'Ac. xv 3' unclear (comma or semicolon)

text: προπετής (of thoughtless haste), impulsive, rash, reckless.
προπορεύομαι, I journey in front, I go before.
gloss: I journey in front, I go before

text: προσάββατον, the day before the Sabbath, i. e. from 6 p.m. on Thursday to 6 p.m. on Friday.
προσαγορεύω, I designate as by addressing by a certain title; I recognize as.
gloss: I designate as by addressing by a certain title

text: προσάγω, (a) (adduco), I lead to, I bring to; characteristically, I bring a subject into the presence of a king), I present to, I introduce, 1 Pet. iii 18; (b) intr. I approach, Ac. xxvii 27 (v. l.).
gloss: I lead to, I bring to
note: closing bracket after 'king' has no opening bracket on the page

text: προσαγωγή, access, entrée, or perhaps a metaphor from the concrete sense landing-stage.
προσαιτέω, I beg, I am a beggar.
gloss: I beg, I am a beggar

text: προσαίτης, a beggar.
προσαναβαίνω, I go up to, I come up to.
gloss: I go up to, I come up to

text: προσαναλίσκω, I spend in addition.
προσαναπληρόω, I fill up by adding, make up, supply.
gloss: I fill up by adding, make up, supply

text: προσανατίθεμαι, I turn (have recourse) to.
προσαπειλέομαι, I add a threat (or threats) to the warning.
gloss: I add a threat (or threats) to the warning

text: προσδαπανάω, I spend in addition.
προσδέομαι, I need (have need of) something additional.
gloss: I need (have need of) something additional

text: προσδοκία, expectation, waiting.
προσεάω, I permit to go straight onwards.
gloss: I permit to go straight onwards

text: προσεργάζομαι, I produce in addition, I gain.
gloss: I produce in addition, I gain

text: προσηλόω, I nail to.
προσήλυτος (lit. that has come to), a proselyte, that is a non-Jew, who has been circumcised and has adopted the Jews' religion.
πρόσκαιρος, for an occasion, transitory.
προσκαρτέρησις, constant attendance, persistence, perseverance, constancy.
προσκεφάλαιον, a pillow or a cushion.
προσκληρόω, I allot (assign) to (as disciples), Ac. xvii 4, where, if the passive has a middle force, we may translate, threw in their lot with.
προσκλίνω, mid. I attach myself to, follow.
πρόσκλισις, inclination; possibly, taking sides, party spirit.
προσκολλάω, (lit. I glue one thing to another), I join (unite) closely: fut. pass. probably as middle, I cleave (to).
note: headword printed as active προσκολλάω; the small mark after it is faint (comma or print flaw)

text: προσκοπή, causing of stumbling (met.).
προσκυλίω, I roll to (up to).
προσκυνητής, a worshipper.
προσλαλέω, I speak to.
πρόσλημψις, taking to one's self; assumption into God's favour.
προσορμίζομαι, I anchor at a place.
προσοφείλω, I owe besides (in addition).
προσοχθίζω, I entertain anger (disgust, abhorrence).
πρόσπεινος, either inclined to hunger or very hungry.
gloss: either inclined to hunger or very hungry

text: προσπήγνυμι, I fix to anything.
προσποιέομαι, I pretend.
προσπορεύομαι, I come to.
προσρήγνυμι, I dash against.
προστάσσω, (a) I instruct, command; (b) I appoint, Ac. xvii 26.
προστάτις (a development of the political sense of προστάτης [patronus], a political sponsor of resident aliens), protectress, patroness.
προστρεχω, I run (run up) to a person.
gloss: I run (run up) to a person
note: no accent visible on the printed headword (προστρεχω); transcribed as printed

text: προσφάγιον, a relish, delicacy, or tit-bit eaten with bread (commonly it would be fish).
gloss: a relish, delicacy, or tit-bit eaten with bread

text: πρόσφατος (from πρός and the root of φόνος, therefore originally newly slaughtered, fresh-killed), now for the first time made, new.
gloss: now for the first time made, new

text: προσφάτως, freshly, recently.
προσφιλής, lovable, amiable.
προσφωνέω, c. acc. I call, I summon: c. dat. I call (out) to; I address, I give a speech to, Ac. xxii 2, cf. absol. Ac. xxi 40.
πρόσχυσις, pouring upon the altar (as was done in later times, not in that of Moses).
προσψαύω, I touch, handle.
προσωπολημπτέω (from προσωπολήμπτης, Hebraistic, later than LXX), I favour specially.
προσωπολήμπτης (from πρόσωπον and λαμβάνειν, Hebraistic, later than LXX; see under the latter), a special favourer of one more than of another, a respecter of persons.
gloss: a special favourer of one more than of another

text: προσωπολημψία (a Hebraistic expression, later than LXX), favouritism, partiality.
προτείνω, I stretch forward, I put into a tense posture.
gloss: I stretch forward, I put into a tense posture

text: προτίθεμαι, I set before myself, I purpose openly: but perhaps, I offer, I provide.
gloss: I set before myself, I purpose openly

text: προτρέπομαι, I encourage.
προτρέχω, I run forward.
προϋπάρχω, I am (previously), I have been already.
gloss: I am (previously), I have been already

text: προφέρω, I bring forth (out), produce.
προφητικός, belonging to a προφήτης or to προφῆται, prophetic.
gloss: belonging to a προφήτης or to προφῆται, prophetic

text: προφῆτις, a prophetess.
προφθάνω, I anticipate, I forestall.
προχειρίζομαι, I appoint, elect (for an important duty).
gloss: I appoint, elect (for an important duty)

text: προχειροτονέω, I appoint beforehand.
Πρόχορος, Prochorus, one of the seven original ‘deacons’ at Jerusalem.
gloss: Prochorus, one of the seven original ‘deacons’ at Jerusalem

text: πρύμνα, the stern of a ship.
πρωΐα, early morning.
πρωϊνός (from πρωΐ) (matutinus), belonging to the morning, morning: opposite ἑσπερινός.
πρῴρα, the prow, the bow of a ship.
gloss: the prow, the bow of a ship
note: headword printed with acute and iota subscript (πρῴρα)

text: πρωτεύω, I hold the first (chief) place, I am the head.
gloss: I hold the first (chief) place, I am the head

text: πρωτοκαθεδρία, the chief (most honourable) seat (chair, stall).
πρωτοκλισία, the chief (most honourable) reclining-place on the dining couches at a dinner table.
πρῶτον (primum), in the first place, first: τὸ πρῶτον (primo), at first, at the beginning.
πρωτοστάτης, one who stands in the front rank, hence a leader, ringleader.
gloss: one who stands in the front rank

text: πρωτοτόκια (τά), one's rights as first-born.
πρωτότοκος, first-born, earliest born, eldest.
πρώτως, for the first time (v. l.).
πταίω, of incipient falling, I trip, stumble, lit. or met.
πτέρνα, heel.
πτερύγιον, the gable, roof, projection of the temple roof, pinnacle; or possibly (see ἱερόν), the wall surrounding the temple precinct.
gloss: the gable, roof, projection of the temple roof, pinnacle

text: πτηνός, winged; hence as substantive, a bird.
πτοέω, I scare, I strike with panic.
gloss: I scare, I strike with panic

text: πτόησις, fear, terror (or other violent excitement).
Πτολεμαΐς, Ptolemaïs, a coast city of Phoenicia, midway between Tyre and Caesarea.
gloss: Ptolemaïs, a coast city of Phoenicia

text: πτύον, a winnowing-fan, a simple wooden pitchfork.
gloss: a winnowing-fan, a simple wooden pitchfork

text: πτύρω, I frighten, terrify.
πτύσμα, spittle.
πτύσσω, I roll up, close.
πτύω, I spit.
πτῶσις, falling, fall.
πτωχεία, (strictly beggary, but rather merely) poverty.
πτωχεύω, I live the life of a poor man.
gloss: I live the life of a poor man

text: πυγμή, the fist: meaning of Mk. vii 3 (v. l.) still uncertain (‘turning the closed fist of one hand about the hollow of the other’, or ‘as far as the elbow’, or paraphrased by ‘diligently’, ‘carefully’?).
πύθων, a ventriloquist (the utterance being supposed to be due to the presence of a familiar spirit [πύθων] within the body of the speaker).
πυκνός, (spissus, thick; hence) frequent: acc. plur. neut. πυκνά as adv., frequently, often (cf. regular comparative of adverb, Ac. xxiv 26).
πυκτεύω, I am a boxer, I box.
gloss: I am a boxer, I box

text: πυρά, a fire.
πύργος, a tower.
πυρέσσω, I have fever, I suffer from fever.
gloss: I have fever, I suffer from fever

text: πυρετός, a fever: medical writers use the plural (Ac. xxviii 8), where we should use the singular, because of recurring attacks of fever.
πύρινος, as of fire, that is, probably, fire-coloured.

πυρόω, (a) I equip with fire, Eph. vi 16 (of flaming darts), I refine by fire, Rev. i 15, iii 18, I burn with fire, I fire, 2 Pet. iii 12; (b) mid. or pass. met., of strong passion or feeling, I burn with fleshly lust, 1 Cor. vii 9; I blaze with anger, 2 Cor. xi 29.
πυρράζω, I am red (ruddy).
Πύρρος, Pyrrhus, father of the Christian Sopater of Beroea.
gloss: Pyrrhus, father of the Christian Sopater of Beroea

text: πυρρός, red.
πύρωσις, (a) burning; (b) met. trial as it were by fire, fiery test, 1 Pet. iv 12.
πώποτε, ever yet, yet at any time, only used after a negative word.
gloss: ever yet, yet at any time

text: πωρόω (from πῶρος, a kind of marble, then, a bony formation on the joints, and a callus or ossification uniting two portions of a fractured bone: thus πωρόω, I petrify, and I cover with a callus, and I deaden, I dull), I make (render) obtuse (dull, dead); I blind (intellectually or morally).

πώρωσις (originally petrifaction, hardness: then the result of this, as metaphorically applied to organs of feeling), insensibility, numbness, obtuseness, dulling of the faculty of perception, deadness; intellectual (moral) blindness.
Ῥαάβ (Hebr.), Rahab, a Canaanitess, who rescued the Hebrew spies at Jericho, by tradition wife of Salmon (Mt. i 4, 5).
ῥαββουνεί (Aramaic, a fuller form of ῥαββεί), my master.
ῥαβδίζω, I flog (beat) with a rod (staff), a Roman punishment.
ῥαβδοῦχος (lictor), (lit. a rod holder, holder of rods), a lictor, an attendant (orderly), of certain Roman magistrates, a tipstaff.
Ῥαγαύ (Hebr.), Ragau, an ancestor of Jesus.
ῥᾳδιούργημα, a moral wrong, a crime.
ῥᾳδιουργία, (ease in working; so unscrupulousness: hence) fraud, wickedness.
ῥακά (or ῥαχά) (Aramaic), empty foolish.
ῥάκος, a piece of cloth.
Ῥαμά; Rama, a place in Ephraim, two hours north of Jerusalem.
gloss: Rama, a place in Ephraim, two hours north of Jerusalem
note: mark after headword looks like a semicolon (possibly a comma with a speck)

text: ῥαντίζω, (a) I sprinkle and thus purify; (b) mid. I sprinkle (purify) myself, Mk. vii 4.
ῥαντισμός, sprinkling, as a symbolic purification (cf. Exod. xxiv 6–8).
ῥαπίζω, I slap, strike.
ῥάπισμα (colaphus), a slap, a blow on the cheek with the open hand.
gloss: a slap, a blow on the cheek with the open hand

text: ῥαφίς, a sewing needle (= classical βελόνη, used by Lk.).
Ῥαχήλ (Hebr.), Rachel, younger wife of the patriarch Jacob.
gloss: Rachel, younger wife of the patriarch Jacob

text: Ῥεβέκκα (Hebr.), Rebecca, wife of the patriarch Isaac.
gloss: Rebecca, wife of the patriarch Isaac

text: ῥέδη (reda, a word of Keltic origin), a carriage.
ῥῆγμα, a breaking up, collapse.
ῥήγνυμι, ῥήσσω, (a) I break: I rend, tear: in Mk. ix 18, Lk. ix 42, it = either σπαράσσω, of convulsions, or I throw on the ground; (b) intr. I break forth into joy, Gal. iv 27.
Ῥησά (Hebr.), Resa, an ancestor of Jesus.
ῥήτωρ, a rhetorician, a professional public speaker; hence, a barrister, acting as counsel for the prosecution.
gloss: a rhetorician, a professional public speaker

text: ῥητῶς, in so many words, expressly, explicitly.
gloss: in so many words, expressly, explicitly

text: ῥιπή, a glance (indicating instantaneousness), flash of an eye.
gloss: a glance (indicating instantaneousness), flash of an eye

text: ῥιπίζω (from ῥιπίς, a fire-fan: hence, I fan either a fire or a person), I raise with the wind.
ῥίπτω (iacio), ῥιπτέω (iacto), I throw, cast; I shake, toss: ἐριμμένοι, sunk powerless, Mt. ix 36: in Ac. xxii 23, I toss about, a sign of excitement and uncontrollable rage.
note: ἐριμμένοι printed with a single ρ and smooth breathing; transcribed as printed

text: Ῥοβοάμ (Hebr.), Rehoboam, son of Solomon, and King of Israel.
gloss: Rehoboam, son of Solomon, and King of Israel

text: Ῥόδη (lit. Rose), Rhoda, a maidservant in the house of John Mark's mother at Jerusalem.
gloss: Rhoda, a maidservant in the house of John Mark's mother

text: Ῥόδος, Rhodes, an island in the Aegean sea, SW. of Asia Minor.
gloss: Rhodes, an island in the Aegean sea

text: ῥοιζηδόν (properly expressing the whizzing sound produced by rapid motion through the air), with thunderous crash (roar).
ῥομφαία (properly a long Thracian sword), a sword, scimitar: met. in Lk. ii 35 of acute suffering.
Ῥουβήν (Hebr.), Reuben, eldest son of the patriarch Jacob and founder of a tribe.
gloss: Reuben, eldest son of the patriarch Jacob

text: Ῥούθ (Hebr.), Ruth, wife of Boes (Boaz) and mother of Iobed (Obed).
gloss: Ruth, wife of Boes (Boaz) and mother of Iobed (Obed)

text: Ῥοῦφος, Rufus, a Christian man in Rome (Rom. xvi 13), probably to be identified with the brother of Alexander and son of Simon of Cyrene mentioned in Mk. xv 21.
gloss: Rufus, a Christian man in Rome

text: ῥύμη, a street or lane in a town or city.
gloss: a street or lane in a town or city
